Jeffrey, Milton and Zeke have a citation for their deaths at 82 Eridani. Nothing names who made them.

A third-generation Hector lost at 82 Eridani and an ~18th-generation Hector emailing Bill in 2343. Either the naming convention broke down or they're two Bobs. Currently two records and the only standing validator warning.

Verne — parentage beyond the appendix

Settled as Bill's clone by the Cast of Characters. The narrative only ever put him on Loki's crew at 82 Eridani, which was suggestive and never stated. Worth a look for a narrative confirmation.

Rebuild born, vessel and designation from the text rather than from the sources we dropped. 17 birth dates, 3 vessels and 43 generation numbers came out in the sweep; some are certainly recoverable by reading around each name.

Neither field has been verified against the text. Starfleet's location data was purged in-world (Bk4 ch32), so expect real gaps there rather than research failures.

Book 2's appendix rescued ten records and turned up Surly. A quick check of the other volumes' back matter is cheap.

Second pass on the moot scenes for later generations

Swept once and declared exhausted, but that was before the parser recovered six chapters. Worth one more pass now the corpus is complete.

[CLEARED] Books restored and the cache guarded

The five ebooks were deleted by a commit-splitting script that ran rm -rf on directories before restoring them from git archive — books/ is gitignored, so nothing came back but .gitkeep. It went unnoticed for hours because .cache/corpus.json survived and every build and test kept passing. Restored from backup 11 Aug 2026. `make corpus` now refuses to overwrite the cache when any book parses to fewer chapters than it already holds, and refuses an empty books/ rather than treating it as an empty corpus; --force overrides. The restored book 1 is the 2016 EPUB rather than the MOBI, which needed a third header detector — see the chapter-parsing notes.

[CLEARED] Browser test harness moved into the repo

Lived in a scratch directory, so it didn't survive a session and its record-count assertions went stale unnoticed — it asserted 86 records for a whole session after the 87th landed. Now tests/ behind `make test`, run against the shipped dist/index.html rather than the template. Expectations are derived from data/*.json instead of hardcoded. Its first run found two live bugs: build.py's ORDER whitelist was silently dropping `alias` and `priorClaim`, so the HAS LEAD chip matched nothing and Will's "/ Riker" never rendered. Includes a golden-master snapshot of 95 states, so the console restructure can be verified by diff.

System map

Largely derivable from origin, visited and lostAt. Sol, Epsilon Eridani, Delta Eridani, 82 Eridani, Omicron² Eridani, Delta and Gamma Pavonis, Eta Cassiopeiae, Poseidon, Gliese 877, HIP 84051, Alpha Centauri, Ragnarök/Valhalla.

Peoples and polities

Deltans, Quinlans, Pav, the Others, Zjentfen; the Pangean Council, the UFS, the Quinlan Resistance and Crew, and the Bawbes. Needs its own schema — species and governments don't have parents, so the tier system won't transfer.

Illustrate the bestiary

Two of nine have art — dragon and kraken, drawn as stroke-only SVG so the console can colour them with currentColor. The rest show a dashed plate with their role mark. Adding one is: draw assets/bestiary/<id>.svg, rebuild. The build refuses art containing a script or an external URL, so the page keeps its promise of zero external requests.

[CLEARED] Bestiary built

Nine creatures in data/bestiary.json, with its own register and an illustration pipeline. The inherited candidate list was mostly wrong — five of eight entries did not survive checking against the text: landers is Dr. Landers, spits is a human faction, boojums are Quinlan drones, hexghi is the Deltan word for a family group, and snarks are Quinlans, who are people. It also missed dragons entirely, at 191 mentions the most-discussed animal in the series. Still to do: a second pass for Ragnarok and Heaven's River river life, and the 'contested sapience' cases the books deliberately leave open.

BOBNET — 4

Star chart: three labels still drop, and two judgement calls open

Gliese 54, Zeta Tucanae and Gliese 877 sit almost on top of each other at the default angle and lose their names to decluttering; rotating separates them. Open questions from the first look: whether the glow is now cut too far, and whether the backdrop at magnitude 6 is too busy behind the systems (5.5 would thin it by 40%). Both are one-line changes.

Galaxy scale view — later

Everything the Bobs reach fits inside 48.8 ly; the galaxy is ~100,000 ly across, so at that scale the whole story is smaller than a pixel. That's the point of it rather than an obstacle — but any Milky Way rendering is an artist's impression, so it belongs in the decoration bucket, clearly marked. Defer until the local chart is finished.

Blog posts in Bill's voice

Bill's blog is canon — he needles Bob about not reading it in Bk4 ch5. Site updates belong as dated posts, not changelogs. See the voice guide in CLAUDE.md.

Images

Later. Whatever we do has to survive the no-external-requests rule, so anything visual gets inlined.

[CLEARED] Console restructured around a register list

Every view used to be hardcoded: five tab buttons in the markup, a ternary chain in render(), and state.view special cases in the dossier, the paint step and the resize handler. Adding a sixth register meant editing all of them. Now REGISTERS drives all five, and a new view is one entry plus one render function. Done as a golden-master refactor — the 95-state snapshot was byte-identical before and after, so nothing rendered differently. tests/registers.test.js adds a synthetic register at runtime and checks every hook fires, so the next state.view special case will fail the build rather than rot quietly.
